notes: Full description: pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs check_revocation() does not verify that the passed 'issuer' Certificate's subject DN matches cert.tbs_certificate.issuer. The CRL checker has a parallel check at crl.rs:202: 'names_match(&issuer.tbs_certificate.subject, &crl.tbs_cert_list.issuer)'. OCSP has no equivalent. The architectural defense is that validate_path already establishes the issuer-to-cert name linkage before check_revocation is called, so a correctly-used API is safe. However the defense-in-depth guarantee documented for CrlChecker (step 2b comment: 'guards against a caller passing a mismatched issuer certificate') is absent from OcspChecker. If a caller passes an incorrect issuer cert, the only catch is the CertID hash check at step 7a (which compares issuer.subject hash against the OCSP response's CertID.issuerNameHash). Fix: Add a check after step (6b): if !names_match(&issuer.tbs_certificate.subject, &cert.tbs_certificate.issuer) { return Err(Error::OcspSignatureInvalid); } Priority: P2 (API misuse gap; not exploitable in normal architectural flow).
title: FINDING: OcspChecker missing cert-issuer identity binding check
